tiers.name: Core
tiers.blurb: The classics every backend interview draws from. Each one teaches a building block you will reuse.

tiers.name: Product systems
tiers.blurb: Real products with real constraints: money, maps, video, inventory.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.blurb: Staff-level problems: strict ordering, streaming at scale, collaboration, exactly-once.

tiers.name: Frontend system design
tiers.blurb: The interview frontend engineers get: components, client state, rendering, network and accessibility.

problems.prompt: We want our own short-link service. People paste a long link, get back something like sho.rt/aZ3kQ9x, and anyone who opens it lands on the original page. Owners also want to see how many clicks each link got.
Our public API runs on about 150 gateway servers. Design the system that limits how many requests each API key, user or IP address can make, so one noisy customer cannot take the platform down.

Every service in our company needs IDs for new rows, messages and events. Design a way to generate unique 64-bit IDs that roughly sort by creation time, across several data centers, without a central bottleneck.

Design a key-value store that holds a few terabytes across many machines, keeps working when machines or a whole zone fail, and lets each application choose between faster responses and fresher reads.

Many teams cache database results in their own ad-hoc ways. Design a shared in-memory cache cluster for the whole company, handling 1.5 million reads per second, that survives node failures and never knocks over the databases behind it.
Build the service every other team calls when they want to tell a user something, by push, SMS or email. It has to respect user preferences, never spam, and not lose the important ones.
Design the home feed for a social app: when I open it, I see recent posts from the people I follow, newest or best first, and I can keep scrolling.
Design a mobile messenger with one-to-one and group chats. Messages should arrive instantly when people are online, wait for them when they are not, and show sent, delivered and read ticks.
As someone types into a search box, show the ten most popular completions for what they have typed so far. Suggestions should reflect what people are actually searching for.
Design a crawler that downloads billions of web pages for a search index and keeps them reasonably fresh, without hammering any website or getting stuck in endless link mazes.
Design a video platform where creators upload videos and viewers anywhere can watch them smoothly on phones, laptops and TVs.
Design a service where people keep a folder of files in sync across their laptop, phone and the web, and can share folders with others.
Design the backend for a ride-hailing app: riders request a car, we find a nearby driver, and both sides watch the trip happen live on a map.
Design a service that shows people restaurants, shops and other places near where they are standing, and lets business owners keep their listings up to date.
Design a live leaderboard for an online game with tens of millions of players: show the top players and tell any player their exact rank right after a match.
Design a site that sells tickets to concerts and sports events, where people pick exact seats and a big on-sale can draw millions of fans in the first few minutes.
Design the booking system for a hotel group: guests search for a room type over a date range, book it, and can cancel later.
Design the system that lets our marketplace take card payments from buyers through an external payment provider and pay sellers later, without ever losing or double-counting money.
Design an internal platform that collects numeric metrics from every service and host in the company, lets engineers graph them, and pages someone when a rule is broken.
Design a shared service where teams register jobs to run once at a set time or on a cron schedule, and the service makes sure each run happens on time, even when machines fail.
Design a mobile photo-sharing app: people upload photos, follow each other, scroll a feed of photos from accounts they follow, and like posts.
Design full-text search over the posts on a large social platform. A user types a few words and gets relevant posts back, including ones written seconds ago.
Design a distributed message log like Kafka. Producers append messages to named topics. Many independent consumer groups read them in order, at their own pace, and can replay history.
Design a system that counts clicks on ads, per ad per minute, for an ad network with billions of clicks a day. Advertisers watch the numbers live, and the same numbers are used to bill them.
Design the 'Trending now' feature of a social platform: show the top 100 hashtags over the last 5 minutes, hour and day, globally and per country, refreshed every few seconds.

Design a document editor where several people can type into the same document at the same time and see each other's changes and cursors live. It should keep full version history and let people keep editing while offline.
Design the core of a stock exchange: brokers send buy and sell orders, the exchange matches them into trades, and everyone gets a live view of the order book. Fairness and speed both matter.
Design live comments and emoji reactions for a live video stream. A big stream can have 10 million people watching at once, and they should see comments and reactions roll in as they happen.
Design a digital wallet where users hold a balance and send money to each other instantly. It must handle tens of thousands of transfers per second, and the books must always balance.
Design an object store like S3: users create buckets and put, get, list and delete files of any size, from a few bytes to terabytes. Data must essentially never be lost.
Build the search box for a large shopping site. As the user types, show up to eight suggestions under the input, and let them pick one with the mouse, touch or keyboard.
Design the web client for a social app's home feed: an endless list of posts with text, photos, likes and comments, which must feel smooth on a mid-range phone.
Design the browser client for a messaging app with one-to-one and group chats. Messages should appear instantly, survive a flaky connection, and unread counts should stay correct.
Design a reusable image carousel for product pages: one big photo at a time, arrows, dots and swipe, used by several teams in the same codebase.

Our company has 25 web apps built by 40 teams, and each has its own buttons, modals and colours. Design the design system and component library they should all share, and tell me how you would get them to adopt it.
